dedupe_keys.name: cu bems smart office building electricity and indoor environment dataset bangkok

description: CU-BEMS is a released set of detailed operation data from a seven-storey, 11,700 square metre office building in Bangkok, Thailand. It gives electricity consumption in kilowatts of the individual air conditioning units, lighting and plug loads in each of the building's 33 zones, together with zone temperature, relative humidity and ambient light measurements, all at one-minute intervals for 18 months from 1 July 2018 to 31 December 2019. The authors list uses including zone, floor and building level load forecasting, indoor thermal model development, validation of building simulation models, demand response algorithms by load type, anomaly detection and reinforcement learning for controlling several air conditioning units. Coverage: one office building in a tropical climate. Access: files linked from the Scientific Data paper, read here through its Europe PMC record because the publisher page did not load. Licence: not stated for the resource; the describing article (doi:10.1038/s41597-020-00582-3) is CC-BY-4.0. Caveats: a single building, and gaps or sensor faults should be checked before use. Simulation uses are control and demand response studies for split air conditioning in hot climates and model calibration. Related records: the Building Data Genome 2.
